loc.hall_of_fates.name: Hall of the Fates
loc.hall_of_fates.description: Outside time itself, the three Moirai spin, measure, and cut the thread of every hero's life. Three great tapestries hang before you, each depicting a different age of heroes.

loc.argo_iolcus.name: Harbor of Iolcus
loc.argo_iolcus.description: The Argo strains at her moorings, fifty oars shipped and ready. King Pelias watches from the cliff above, having sent Jason after the Golden Fleece hoping he would never return.

loc.argo_lemnos.name: Island of Lemnos
loc.argo_lemnos.description: An island of women alone, ruled by Queen Hypsipyle since they rose up against their husbands. The Argonauts have lingered here far longer than the winds allow.

loc.argo_bebrycia.name: Shore of the Bebrycians
loc.argo_bebrycia.description: King Amycus, proud of his skill with the boxer's leather straps, blocks every crew that lands until their best fighter has faced him.

loc.argo_salmydessus.name: Salmydessus, Coast of Thrace
loc.argo_salmydessus.description: The blind seer Phineus sits at a table of rotting food, tormented daily by Harpies who swoop down to foul his meals as punishment from the gods.

loc.argo_symplegades.name: The Clashing Rocks
loc.argo_symplegades.description: The Symplegades grind together at the mouth of the Bosphorus, crushing any ship that dares the passage. Phineus's advice was to release a dove first, and follow if she survives.

loc.argo_colchis_shore.name: Mouth of the River Phasis
loc.argo_colchis_shore.description: The Argo has reached Colchis at last, at the far eastern edge of the known sea, beneath the shadow of the Caucasus mountains.

loc.argo_court_aeetes.name: Court of King Aeetes
loc.argo_court_aeetes.description: King Aeetes, son of the sun god Helios, receives the Argonauts with cold courtesy and a challenge he is certain no mortal can survive.

loc.argo_bull_field.name: Field of the Bronze Bulls
loc.argo_bull_field.description: Two fire-breathing bulls with hooves of bronze must be yoked and set to plow this field, and the dragon's teeth sown in its furrows will rise as armed warriors before nightfall.

loc.argo_grove.name: Sacred Grove of Ares
loc.argo_grove.description: An ancient oak stands at the grove's heart, the Golden Fleece draped over its lowest branch, coiled about by a serpent that has never once closed its eyes.

loc.argo_flight.name: Flight from Colchis
loc.argo_flight.description: The Argo runs before the wind with the Fleece aboard, King Aeetes's warships closing fast behind, led by his own son.

loc.argo_return_sea.name: The Long Way Home
loc.argo_return_sea.description: Driven far from the direct route by an angry Zeus, the Argo threads unfamiliar seas, guided at times by the sea-nymph Thetis herself.

loc.argo_crete.name: Shore of Crete
loc.argo_crete.description: Talos, the bronze giant forged by Hephaestus, strides the beach hurling boulders at any ship that nears the island he was set to guard.

loc.troy_ida.name: Slopes of Mount Ida
loc.troy_ida.description: Here the shepherd-prince Paris judged which goddess was fairest, and Aphrodite's promised reward — the most beautiful woman alive — set the whole war in motion.

loc.troy_sparta.name: Palace of Sparta
loc.troy_sparta.description: King Menelaus's halls stand strangely quiet. His wife Helen sailed for Troy with a guest he had welcomed under his own roof.

loc.troy_aulis.name: Harbor of Aulis
loc.troy_aulis.description: A thousand ships sit becalmed, waiting on winds that will not turn until the seer Calchas is satisfied that the goddess Artemis has been answered.

loc.troy_camp.name: Greek Camp Before Troy
loc.troy_camp.description: Ten years into the siege, rows of black ships line the beach. Agamemnon's quarrel with Achilles over the captive Briseis still poisons the camp.

loc.troy_achilles_tent.name: Tent of Achilles
loc.troy_achilles_tent.description: The greatest of the Greek spearmen sits apart from the war he refuses to fight, his anger at Agamemnon burning hotter than the siege itself.

loc.troy_plain.name: The Scamander Plain
loc.troy_plain.description: Chariots and spearmen clash on the plain between camp and city, the river Scamander running red more days than not.

loc.troy_gate.name: The Scaean Gate
loc.troy_gate.description: Beneath Troy's great gate, Hector holds the line his city cannot survive without, while Helen watches the battle from the walls above.

loc.troy_countryside.name: Fields Beneath the Walls
loc.troy_countryside.description: Chariot tracks scar the ground where Hector's body was once dragged in circles before the horrified eyes of the city.

loc.troy_city.name: Priam's Palace
loc.troy_city.description: Within the walls, aged King Priam rules a city that has buried too many sons, while his daughter Cassandra's warnings go unheeded as always.

loc.troy_horse.name: The Shore of the Horse
loc.troy_horse.description: A hollow horse of fir planking rises on the beach where the Greek ships once stood, Odysseus's answer to ten years of failed sieges.

loc.troy_fall.name: The Burning of Troy
loc.troy_fall.description: The horse was dragged inside the gates as an offering, and by night its hidden crew opened the city to the waiting Greek army. Troy burns.

loc.ody_troy_shore.name: Departure from Troy
loc.ody_troy_shore.description: With Troy fallen, Odysseus turns his ships toward Ithaca, not yet knowing the voyage home will take ten more years than the war itself.

loc.ody_cicones.name: Ismarus, Land of the Cicones
loc.ody_cicones.description: A raid meant to resupply the fleet lingers too long celebrating, and the Cicones return with reinforcements before the ships can escape.

loc.ody_lotus.name: Land of the Lotus-Eaters
loc.ody_lotus.description: Whoever tastes the honeyed lotus fruit forgets home entirely, content to stay forever. Several crewmen already wear the same drowsy smile.

loc.ody_cyclops.name: Cave of Polyphemus
loc.ody_cyclops.description: A stone the size of a hillside seals the cave mouth. Polyphemus, the one-eyed son of Poseidon, has already made a meal of two of the crew.

loc.ody_aeolus.name: The Floating Island of Aeolus
loc.ody_aeolus.description: Aeolus, keeper of the winds by Zeus's own appointment, offers a leather bag holding every wind but the one needed to sail home.

loc.ody_laestrygonians.name: Harbor of the Laestrygonians
loc.ody_laestrygonians.description: Giant cannibals hurl boulders down from the cliffs onto the harbor below, shattering every ship but the one Odysseus was wise enough to anchor outside.

loc.ody_circe.name: Aeaea, Isle of Circe
loc.ody_circe.description: The enchantress Circe has already turned half the landing party into swine rooting in her sty. Smoke curls invitingly from her stone hall all the same.

loc.ody_underworld.name: The House of the Dead
loc.ody_underworld.description: At the world's edge, where the rivers of the underworld meet, the shades of the dead crowd toward a trench of sacrificial blood, eager to speak.

loc.ody_sirens.name: Rocks of the Sirens
loc.ody_sirens.description: Bones litter the rocks below a song so beautiful that every sailor who has heard it clearly has also died hearing it.

loc.ody_scylla.name: The Strait of Scylla and Charybdis
loc.ody_scylla.description: On one side a six-headed monster snatches sailors from the deck; on the other, a whirlpool swallows the sea itself three times a day.

loc.ody_thrinacia.name: Thrinacia, Isle of the Sun
loc.ody_thrinacia.description: Helios pastures his immortal cattle here, bright as sunlight, and swore ruin on any sailor who touches so much as one.

loc.ody_calypso.name: Ogygia, Isle of Calypso
loc.ody_calypso.description: The nymph Calypso has kept the shipwrecked Odysseus at her side for seven years, offering an undying life he keeps refusing.

loc.ody_phaeacia.name: Scheria, Land of the Phaeacians
loc.ody_phaeacia.description: Princess Nausicaa found a shipwrecked, salt-crusted stranger on this shore and brought him to her father's court, where he finally tells his whole story.

loc.ody_ithaca_shore.name: Shore of Ithaca
loc.ody_ithaca_shore.description: Home at last, disguised as a beggar by Athena's hand, Odysseus is welcomed at the hut of his old swineherd Eumaeus before anyone else recognizes him.

loc.ody_palace.name: Hall of the Suitors
loc.ody_palace.description: A hundred suitors feast on Odysseus's own cattle while courting his wife Penelope, who has set them one last, impossible test: string the great bow.

item.hospitality_gift.name: Woven Cloak of Lemnos
item.hospitality_gift.description: A finely woven cloak, a parting gift from the women of Lemnos.

item.medeas_draught.name: Medea's Sleeping Draught
item.medeas_draught.description: A potion brewed from grave-herbs, strong enough to close a dragon's sleepless eyes.

item.dragons_teeth.name: Dragon's Teeth
item.dragons_teeth.description: Teeth drawn from the slain guardian dragon of Ares, said to grow into armed warriors when sown.

item.golden_fleece.name: The Golden Fleece
item.golden_fleece.description: The shining pelt of the ram Chrysomallos, which once carried Phrixus safely across the sea.

item.aulis_offering.name: White Hind of Aulis
item.aulis_offering.description: An offering sent in place of a king's daughter, if the old stories are kind to Agamemnon.

item.shield_of_achilles.name: Shield of Achilles
item.shield_of_achilles.description: Forged by Hephaestus at the sea-nymph Thetis's plea, its rim shows the whole world in bronze, tin, silver, and gold.

item.hectors_ransom.name: Hector's Ransom
item.hectors_ransom.description: A king's weight in gold and fine cloth, Priam's price for the return of his son's body.

item.trojan_horse.name: The Trojan Horse
item.trojan_horse.description: A hollow horse of fir planking, tall as the city walls, with a rope ladder coiled in its belly.

item.olive_stake.name: Sharpened Olive Stake
item.olive_stake.description: A great stake of green olive wood, hardened in the fire and sharpened to a point.

item.strong_wine.name: Unwatered Wine
item.strong_wine.description: Wine strong enough to fell a god, carried ashore from the ship's stores.

item.bag_of_winds.name: Bag of the Winds
item.bag_of_winds.description: A leather bag holding every wind but the one already loosed to carry the ship home. Best left unopened.

item.moly.name: Moly Root
item.moly.description: A small herb with white flowers and a black root, a gift from Hermes proof against any enchantment of Circe's.

item.sacred_cattle.name: Cattle of Helios
item.sacred_cattle.description: One of the sun god's own immortal cattle, coat bright as noon. Touching it is forbidden.

item.odysseus_bow.name: Odysseus's Bow
item.odysseus_bow.description: A great bow that no suitor could even bend, let alone string. It has waited twenty years for its owner's return.

npc.hypsipyle.name: Queen Hypsipyle
npc.hypsipyle.description: Queen of Lemnos, ruling an island of women alone.
dialogue: Stay with us, Argonauts. Lemnos has been lonely since the men were... gone.

npc.amycus.name: King Amycus
npc.amycus.description: The boastful boxer-king of the Bebrycians.
dialogue: No ship passes my shore until its best man faces me in the ring!

npc.phineus.name: Phineus
npc.phineus.description: A blind prophet, tormented eternally by Harpies for a false prophecy.
dialogue: Drive off the Harpies that torment me, and I will tell you how to pass the Clashing Rocks.

npc.harpy.name: Harpy
npc.harpy.description: A winged tormentor sent to foul Phineus's every meal.
dialogue: Screeching, it dives for the old man's plate again.

npc.aeetes.name: King Aeetes
npc.aeetes.description: King of Colchis, son of the sun god Helios, keeper of the Golden Fleece.
dialogue: Yoke my bronze bulls, sow the dragon's teeth, and survive what grows from them — then, perhaps, the Fleece is yours.

npc.khalkotauroi.name: The Bronze Bulls
npc.khalkotauroi.description: Fire-breathing bulls with hooves of bronze, Aeetes's first trial.
dialogue: The bulls snort fire and paw the earth, daring anyone to yoke them.

npc.earthborn.name: Earthborn Warrior
npc.earthborn.description: An armed warrior sprung fully grown from a sown dragon's tooth.
dialogue: It claws free of the soil already reaching for a spear.

npc.medea.name: Medea
npc.medea.description: Princess of Colchis and sorceress, who falls for Jason against her own family's interest.
dialogue: Take this draught — it will close the dragon's eyes. Know that in helping you, I betray my own father.

npc.colchis_dragon.name: The Sleepless Dragon
npc.colchis_dragon.description: A serpent coiled endlessly about the oak that holds the Golden Fleece.
dialogue: Not once, in all its long watch, have its eyes closed.

npc.apsyrtus.name: Apsyrtus
npc.apsyrtus.description: Medea's brother, sent by King Aeetes to reclaim the Fleece and his sister.
dialogue: Sister, come home, and bring the thief who stole our Fleece.

npc.talos.name: Talos
npc.talos.description: A bronze automaton forged by Hephaestus to guard Crete, vulnerable only at a single sealed vein in his ankle.
dialogue: It hurls another boulder the size of a chariot toward the shore.

npc.paris.name: Paris
npc.paris.description: The Trojan prince who judged Aphrodite fairest and was promised the world's most beautiful woman.
dialogue: I chose beauty over the rule of Asia, or the glory of war. Some say that choice will burn a city.

npc.menelaus.name: Menelaus
npc.menelaus.description: King of Sparta, husband of Helen, wronged host and gathering king.
dialogue: She was here, and then she was gone, taken by a guest I welcomed under my own roof.

npc.calchas.name: Calchas
npc.calchas.description: The seer whose reading of the winds and the gods binds the fleet to Aulis.
dialogue: The winds will not turn until Artemis is answered. Bring an offering worthy of a goddess.

npc.agamemnon.name: Agamemnon
npc.agamemnon.description: High King of the Greeks, whose pride cost him his best warrior's spear.
dialogue: Achilles sulks in his tent like a child. The war does not wait for one man's pride.

npc.achilles.name: Achilles
npc.achilles.description: The greatest of the Greek warriors, wrathful and grieving, sitting out the war over a stolen captive.
dialogue: Agamemnon took what was mine to take. Let Hector burn the ships before I lift my spear for his sake.

npc.hector.name: Hector
npc.hector.description: Troy's greatest defender, who will not abandon his city though he knows his fate.
dialogue: Every day I hold this gate is a day my city still stands.

npc.helen.name: Helen
npc.helen.description: The most famous of women, watching the war fought over her from the walls of Troy.
dialogue: I watch my two husbands from these walls — the one I left, and the one who dies defending the roof that hides me.

npc.priam.name: Priam
npc.priam.description: The aged King of Troy, father of Hector, who will kneel before his son's killer for the sake of a proper burial.
dialogue: Achilles dragged my son around these very walls. I will kneel before my enemy if it brings Hector home.

npc.cassandra.name: Cassandra
npc.cassandra.description: Priam's daughter, cursed to see the truth and never be believed.
dialogue: The horse on the shore will bring our end. No one in this city has ever believed me, and no one ever will.

npc.odysseus.name: Odysseus
npc.odysseus.description: The cunning king of Ithaca, architect of the wooden horse.
dialogue: Ten years of spears and walls taught us nothing. So we offer Troy a gift they cannot resist bringing inside their own gates.

npc.aeneas.name: Aeneas
npc.aeneas.description: A Trojan prince fleeing the burning city with his father on his back and his household gods in his arms.
dialogue: Troy falls tonight. Somewhere west of here, I am told, there is another city waiting to be born.

npc.lotus_eater.name: Lotus-Eater
npc.lotus_eater.description: A drowsy islander offering the honeyed fruit that erases every memory of home.
dialogue: Eat the lotus, stranger. Why sail home to grow old, when here there is only honeyed forgetting?

npc.trapped_sailor.name: Trapped Sailor
npc.trapped_sailor.description: A crewman sealed in the cyclops's cave, urging swift action before more of the crew are eaten.
dialogue: Blind the beast before he eats us all one by one — he has already crushed two of our friends against these stones!

npc.polyphemus.name: Polyphemus
npc.polyphemus.description: The one-eyed son of Poseidon, keeper of a cave full of trapped sailors.
dialogue: Nobody is hurting me! Nobody!

npc.aeolus.name: Aeolus
npc.aeolus.description: Keeper of the winds by Zeus's appointment, master of a floating island.
dialogue: Take this bag — the west wind alone is loosed to carry you home. Do not open it before Ithaca.

npc.laestrygonian.name: Laestrygonian Giant
npc.laestrygonian.description: A cannibal giant of Lamos's city, hurling boulders the size of ships.
dialogue: It roars down from the cliff, already reaching for another boulder.

npc.circe.name: Circe
npc.circe.description: The enchantress of Aeaea, daughter of Helios, keeper of a sty full of transformed sailors.
dialogue: Eat the moly root first, and my cup will only make you stronger, never smaller.

npc.tiresias.name: Tiresias
npc.tiresias.description: The blind prophet of Thebes, whose shade is consulted even in death.
dialogue: You will reach home, Odysseus, but only if your men leave the cattle of Helios untouched on Thrinacia.

npc.elpenor.name: Elpenor
npc.elpenor.description: The youngest of the crew, who fell from Circe's roof and died before he could say goodbye.
dialogue: Leave me not unwept, unburied. Burn my body on the shore of Aeaea and raise my oar over the mound.

npc.sirens.name: The Sirens
npc.sirens.description: Singers whose voices have drawn every ship that ever heard them onto the rocks.
dialogue: Come closer, famous Odysseus, and hear the song no man has heard and lived to tell.

npc.scylla.name: Scylla
npc.scylla.description: A six-headed monster of the strait, opposite the whirlpool Charybdis.
dialogue: Six heads lunge from the rock face as the ship draws near.

npc.eurylochus.name: Eurylochus
npc.eurylochus.description: Odysseus's second-in-command, who will lead a starving crew to slaughter the sacred cattle against every warning.
dialogue: Better to die once, quickly, with a full belly, than waste away obeying a warning from a blind old ghost.

npc.calypso.name: Calypso
npc.calypso.description: The nymph who kept Odysseus seven years on Ogygia, offering an undying life at her side.
dialogue: Seven years I offered you a god's own life, deathless and unaging. And still you build a raft to leave me for a mortal wife.

npc.nausicaa.name: Nausicaa
npc.nausicaa.description: Princess of the Phaeacians, who found the shipwrecked Odysseus washed ashore.
dialogue: My mother says: give the stranger clothes, food, and passage. My mother is rarely wrong.

npc.alcinous.name: King Alcinous
npc.alcinous.description: King of the Phaeacians, host to Odysseus, who will provide the ship home.
dialogue: Tell us your story from the beginning, stranger. My court has never heard a tale like yours.

npc.eumaeus.name: Eumaeus
npc.eumaeus.description: The loyal swineherd who shelters the disguised beggar-king without knowing who he shelters.
dialogue: Twenty years I've kept his pigs and his house in order, hoping.

npc.telemachus.name: Telemachus
npc.telemachus.description: Odysseus's son, grown to manhood defending his father's house from the suitors.
dialogue: I was a baby when you sailed. I have grown up defending a house full of men who want my mother's hand and my inheritance both.

npc.antinous.name: Antinous
npc.antinous.description: The most arrogant of Penelope's suitors, feasting nightly on another man's cattle.
dialogue: Another cup, and another of the beggar-king's own oxen for the fire!

npc.penelope.name: Penelope
npc.penelope.description: Odysseus's wife, who wove and unwove a burial shroud for three years to delay remarriage.
dialogue: Twenty years I have waited. Only one man alive could string that bow.

quest.phineus_harpies.name: The Blind Prophet's Torment
quest.phineus_harpies.description: Drive off the Harpy tormenting Phineus, so he will share his knowledge of the Clashing Rocks.

quest.golden_fleece.name: The Golden Fleece
quest.golden_fleece.description: Take the Golden Fleece from the sacred oak, with Medea's help against its sleepless guardian.

quest.wind_offering.name: The Winds of Aulis
quest.wind_offering.description: Bring Calchas an offering worthy of Artemis, so the fleet may finally sail for Troy.

quest.arms_of_achilles.name: The Arms of Achilles
quest.arms_of_achilles.description: Bring Achilles the new armor forged by Hephaestus, so he will return to the war after Patroclus's death.

quest.ransom_hector.name: Ransom of Hector
quest.ransom_hector.description: Deliver Priam's ransom in exchange for the return of Hector's body.

quest.trojan_horse.name: The Wooden Horse
quest.trojan_horse.description: Help Odysseus complete the horse that will finally bring down Troy's walls from within.

quest.blind_the_cyclops.name: Nobody's Escape
quest.blind_the_cyclops.description: Blind Polyphemus to free the crew trapped in his cave.

quest.winds_of_aeolus.name: The Bag of Winds
quest.winds_of_aeolus.description: Accept Aeolus's bag of winds, and guard it well until Ithaca is in sight.

quest.moly_herb.name: The Moly Root
quest.moly_herb.description: Take the moly root before drinking from Circe's cup, or join the pigs in her sty.

quest.sacred_cattle.name: The Forbidden Cattle
quest.sacred_cattle.description: Eurylochus would slaughter the cattle of Helios against every warning. What you do with them is yours to decide.

quest.string_the_bow.name: The Test of the Bow
quest.string_the_bow.description: Take up Odysseus's bow, which no suitor could even bend, and prove who has truly come home.
